instructions: Choose one response for each statement. Consider the past month unless the statement asks about earlier or longstanding patterns. Current or past concerns select areas for age-appropriate follow-up. Unsure and private responses need a clinician's review and are not counted as No. This original questionnaire does not diagnose a condition.

safety.text: In the past month, have you thought about ending your life, not wanting to be alive or hurting yourself on purpose?
In the past month, have you thought about or wanted to seriously hurt someone else?
Right now, are you worried that you might act on harmful thoughts or cannot keep yourself or someone else safe?

domains.title: Attention, learning and social communication
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: I have trouble paying attention, staying organized or managing my activity at school or at home.
Reading, writing, mathematics or learning everyday skills has been difficult for me for a long time.
Social communication, sensory experiences or repeated routines are difficult for me and I would like support.

domains.title: Unusual perceptions and beliefs
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details. Consider experiences while fully awake; ordinary imaginative play and culturally shared beliefs alone do not indicate a disorder.

questions.text: When I am fully awake, I hear, see or sense things that other people do not seem to notice.
I feel watched, controlled or threatened in a way that is hard to explain to people I trust.
My thoughts get so mixed up that I have trouble talking clearly or getting everyday things done.

domains.title: Periods of unusually high energy
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: I have had a period when my mood and energy were much higher or more irritable than usual for me.
During a high-energy period, I slept much less than usual without feeling tired.
During a high-energy period, my fast thoughts, talking or risky choices worried me or other people.

domains.title: Low mood and loss of interest
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: I feel sad, empty, hopeless or unusually irritable much of the time.
I am less interested in friends, hobbies or other things I usually enjoy.
Low mood or strong self-criticism makes school, home life or everyday tasks harder.

domains.title: Worry, fear and panic
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: Worry or fear is hard for me to control.
I have sudden spells of strong fear or panic, sometimes with a racing heart or trouble catching my breath.
Fear makes me avoid school, friends, activities or being away from people I depend on.

domains.title: Intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviors
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: Unwanted thoughts, pictures or urges keep coming into my mind and are hard to set aside.
I feel I must repeat actions or mental routines, such as checking, washing, counting or asking for reassurance.
Saving things, worries about appearance, skin picking or hair pulling causes problems or distress for me.

domains.title: Reactions to trauma and major stress
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: After something frightening or overwhelming, upsetting memories or nightmares come back when I do not want them.
After a difficult experience, I avoid reminders, feel cut off or stay very watchful or easily startled.
After a major change, stress or loss, my feelings or behavior make everyday life harder.

domains.title: Detachment and gaps in awareness
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: I sometimes feel disconnected from my body or feelings, or things around me seem unreal.
I cannot remember important events or chunks of time beyond ordinary forgetting.
Changes in my sense of who I am or what is happening leave me confused or distressed.

domains.title: Physical symptoms and health-related distress
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details. Physical symptoms need appropriate medical attention; do not assume they are psychological.

questions.text: Physical symptoms make school, activities or daily life difficult.
I spend a lot of time worrying about my health or sensations in my body.
Checking symptoms, asking for reassurance or avoiding things because of health worries is hard to manage.

domains.title: Eating and body-related concerns
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: I eat too little or avoid foods in a way that could affect my growth, health or daily life.
Eating feels out of control, or I try to undo eating by vomiting, misusing medicine or exercising too much.
Worries about food or body size, or eating things that are not food, cause problems for me.

domains.title: Bladder and bowel concerns
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: I have repeated wetting or trouble controlling urine, including while asleep.
I have repeated soiling or trouble controlling bowel movements.
Bladder or bowel difficulties make me avoid activities or feel worried or embarrassed.

domains.title: Sleep and daytime alertness
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: I have trouble falling asleep, staying asleep or waking when I need to.
I am very sleepy during the day or still feel tired after enough time in bed.
Breathing problems, unusual movements or behaviors in sleep, or my sleep schedule worry me or affect my day.

domains.title: Body development and private well-being
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details. Do not record explicit details. This is a support screen, not an adult sexual-function assessment.

questions.text: I have private questions or worries about puberty, changes in my body or sexual well-being that I want to discuss with a clinician.
Pain or physical discomfort involving private parts of my body concerns me.
Worries about my body or sexual well-being interfere with everyday life or make me want help.

domains.title: Gender-related distress and support
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details. Gender identity or expression is not itself a symptom; these questions concern distress and requested support.

questions.text: I feel distressed because aspects of my body or assigned sex do not fit my experience of my gender.
Being treated as a gender that does not fit my experience upsets me.
I want support with gender-related stress, pressure, bullying or discrimination.

domains.title: Anger and impulse control
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: I have anger outbursts or aggressive actions that feel hard to control.
I act on urges in ways that hurt myself, other people, property or things I need to do.
Repeated serious conflicts, lying or rule breaking cause problems at home, school or elsewhere.

domains.title: Alcohol, drugs and gambling
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: I use alcohol, nicotine, cannabis, other drugs or medicine in a way that is hard to control.
Using substances, wanting to use them or feeling unwell without them affects my health, safety, school or relationships.
Gambling or betting feels hard to control or has caused problems.

domains.title: Changes in thinking and previously learned skills
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details.

questions.text: My memory, attention or thinking has become worse than it used to be.
Changes in speaking, understanding, judgment or finding my way make everyday tasks harder.
I or someone who knows me well has noticed confusion or trouble doing things I could do before.

domains.title: Developing coping and relationship patterns
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details. This does not assign a personality disorder; developmental context and clinical review are essential.

questions.text: Patterns of conflict, mistrust or pulling away keep causing problems in my relationships.
Managing strong feelings, impulses or my sense of who I am is difficult across situations.
I keep coping in ways that hurt relationships or school or home responsibilities, and I want help changing them.

domains.title: Body boundaries and sexual safety
domains.instructions: Think about school, home, friendships and activities. You may choose a private discussion instead of giving details. Do not record explicit details. This does not assign a paraphilic diagnosis or infer abuse; discuss concerns directly with a qualified clinician.

questions.text: Sexual thoughts, urges or experiences cause distress or make daily life difficult, and I want a private discussion.
I worry that I might cross another person's sexual boundaries or do something without their agreement.
I want help staying safe, respecting boundaries or managing sexual thoughts or urges.
